subject: Request: targeted session snapshot preservation and deletion delegation
messages:
From: Mark Ellis <mark.ellis@pinewoodhealth.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: security@pinewoodhealth.com
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Preservation request: tenant X session snapshots for incident triage

Avery —

We briefed our incident response team this morning and need Redwood's help to preserve a narrow set of session-level artifacts for a 90-day investigation window. Scope below: 

- Tenant: pinewood-prod (tenant_id: pinewood-57)
- Objects: full session snapshots (request/response payloads), timestamped session metadata, and the minimal set of ephemeral logs that map session_id -> worker instance for forensic tracing.
- Time range: all sessions touching the suspect endpoint between 2027-08-02 and 2027-08-10.
- Purpose: internal incident triage and regulatory review; we may need export bundles with integrity hashes and a short audit manifest for SOC evidencing.

We understand Redwood's standard retention is 30 days for session payloads. This is a customer-specific preservation request tied to an ongoing investigation and the CAIQ item 3.5. Could you confirm:

1) Can Redwood isolate and hold only the listed objects for the specified tenant and timeframe?
2) Will the preserved snapshots be retained encrypted and stored separately from general logs?
3) What is the expected turnaround for providing an export bundle (manifest + checksums) once we submit a formal PO or amended SOW?
4) Do you require a signed addendum / preservation agreement before you begin the hold?

I've attached a short incident overview to give context. Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Mark Ellis
CISO, Pinewood Health
mark.ellis@pinewoodhealth.com
(415) 555-0182
Attachment: pinewood_incident_overview.pdf

Next steps I propose:
- Neha: confirm technical feasibility and what will be preserved exactly.
- Stephanie: confirm contract/addendum needed and whether an accelerated SOW amendment is required.
- Mark: if you can confirm the exact session_id list (or a query to identify them) and whether you need nightly exports during the 90-day window, that helps sizing.

I'll also attach the short Redwood retention summary so everyone has the baseline policy.

Best,

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Cc: Mark Ellis <mark.ellis@pinewoodhealth.com>, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com

Subject: RE: Preservation request: tenant X session snapshots for incident triage

Mark / Avery / Stephanie —

Thanks for flagging this. Technical summary and constraints below. TL;DR: We can do a tenant-scoped preservation for the requested time range, but it requires an operational run (export + sealed storage) and a brief contract addendum. Details: 

What we can preserve (hosted Redwood):
- Session snapshots: full request/response payloads tied to session_id. These are normally ephemeral but can be bottled into a separate, encrypted archive for a defined retention window.
- Session metadata: timestamps, IP blocks (redacted on request), worker/instance mapping, and delivery traces.
- Minimal mapping logs: we will extract only the indices that map session_id -> compute node for forensic reconstruction; we will not preserve full system-level logs unless requested.

Operational notes:
- Storage: preserved bundles are stored encrypted at rest in a siloed bucket (region us-west-2 by default). Access is IAM-restricted to the Redwood Security Team and the designated customer designees.
- Integrity: we provide SHA-256 checksums and a manifest file listing objects + provenance details.
- Encryption keys: customer may elect to use Redwood-managed keys or provide a CMK (KMS) for the preserved artifacts; HSM-backed KMS is possible but will add ~48-72 hours to setup.
- Turnaround: from signed addendum + PO, standard run to package the requested window is 3 business days; expedited 24–48 hour options are available for an additional ops fee.
- Deletion/delegation: after the preservation window we can either (a) delete artifacts, (b) rotate to a longer-term escrow, or (c) transfer an encrypted export package to the customer (SFTP / secure transfer). Decision must be documented in the addendum.

Limitations / items needing confirmation:
1) Exact selector: we need either a list of session_ids OR the precise query (e.g., endpoint=/api/v1/charge AND status=500 AND timestamp between X and Y). Generic descriptions are hard for accurate exports.
2) Private deployment nuance: if Pinewood runs on Redwood Private (customer-managed infra), we will provide tooling + runbook but the export must be executed by the customer's infra team under Redwood guidance.
3) Legal hold vs. retention: a preservation addendum is different than changing default retention – we will not change global policy; this is a scoped hold tied to the incident.

Required paperwork:
- Short one-page preservation addendum (we draft)
- PO or SOW amendment to cover ops time and any escrow/transfer fees

I'll attach our internal preservation runbook to show the exact artifact names and manifest format. Once you confirm the selector and who will be the customer designee for retrieval requests, we can draft the addendum and schedule the run.

Neha Kapoor
Security Lead, Platform Compliance
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Attachment: preservation_runbook.md

Avery / Neha / Stephanie —

Thanks, all — that is exactly the level of detail we needed. Confirming next steps from Pinewood: 

- We will provide the precise session_id list (CSV) by EOD Monday 2027-08-16.
- We elect Redwood-managed KMS for the preserved artifacts to avoid onboarding delays; please call out the ops fee for expedited packaging in the addendum.
- We want nightly incremental exports during the 90-day window pushed to a secure SFTP where our IR team can pull nightly bundles. Please include the SFTP transfer option in the SOW (and any associated egress costs).
- Our legal team will review your draft preservation addendum. We will need a signature prior to you beginning any export or hold.

If you can draft the addendum and the PO line items for standard vs expedited packaging + nightly transfer costs, we can accelerate. We may also need a short statement confirming that preserved artifacts will not be used for model training or product telemetry analysis — that language is commonly requested in our CAIQ responses.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Mark
CISO, Pinewood Health
